note: Auditable alert-to-action rules. Personal rules are only evaluated while the detector has an open alert, so the false-alert budget is set by the detector, not by these rules. u = mean deviation over the last three measured days, in robust standard deviations, in the direction of concern.

rules.title: Symptom that needs the medical officer now
rules.summary: You reported a symptom that should never wait for a trend. Keel does not interpret it.
rules.action: Tell the crew medical officer now.
steps: Stop exercise and any demanding task.
Stay with another crew member.
The medical officer runs the onboard medical checklist; Keel queues a summary for the ground for when a link is available.
rules.tier_reason: Red-flag symptom: medical officer now, ground as soon as a link exists.

rules.title: Radiation dose rate is far above normal
rules.summary: Today's dose rate is several times the mission's usual level, which is what a solar particle event looks like.
rules.action: Follow the solar storm shelter procedure with the whole crew.
steps: End or delay any spacewalk.
Move to the most shielded area; build the shelter from stowage if the vehicle uses one.
Keep personal dosimeters on. Keel keeps tracking the mission total against the career limit.
rules.tier_reason: Crew-wide environmental exposure: commander and medical officer are informed automatically.

rules.title: Cabin carbon dioxide is elevated
rules.summary: The three-day average is above 3.0 mmHg, the level ISS operations adopted as a limit after crews reported headaches and slips at higher levels.
rules.action: Check the air revitalization system and move work and sleep to a better ventilated spot.
steps: Commander or engineer: check scrubber status and fan airflow.
Avoid enclosed corners where air pools; raise local ventilation in sleep stations.
Log any headache at check-in so the link to air quality is visible.
Use buddy checks on procedures until the level is back down.
rules.tier_reason: Crew-wide environmental issue: commander and medical officer are informed automatically.

rules.title: Expected adaptation to the new gravity level
rules.summary: Nausea and dizziness in the first days after a gravity change are expected in most crew and usually pass within two to three days. Keel has widened your normal ranges for this period.
rules.action: Take it easy today: slow head movements, light duty, small sips and snacks.
steps: Tell the medical officer if you cannot keep fluids down or if it lasts beyond day 4.

escalate.reason: Lasting longer than the usual two to three days.

rules.title: Your body looks like it is under strain
rules.summary: Resting heart rate is up together with other recovery signals. This combination is often seen in the days before or during an infection, but Keel cannot tell you the cause.
rules.action: Take your temperature now, swap today's hard exercise for a light session, and tell the medical officer.
steps: Repeat temperature in four hours and log symptoms at check-in.
Drink to your fluid target and protect tonight's sleep period.
Keep some distance at meals and wipe shared surfaces until this clears.
If temperature is 38.0 °C or higher, or you feel worse, the medical officer should see you today.
rules.tier_reason: Possible illness in a closed cabin affects the whole crew, and early rest is cheap.

escalate.reason: High temperature deviation or no improvement after four days: queue for the flight surgeon.

rules.title: Blood oxygen is below your normal
rules.summary: Your overnight blood oxygen has been lower than your own range.
rules.action: Take a fingertip reading now, sitting still with a warm hand.
steps: If the resting reading is 92% or lower, or you are short of breath, tell the medical officer now.
Check the cabin carbon dioxide and oxygen readings.
If the reading is normal, wear the sensor snugly tonight and compare tomorrow.
rules.tier_reason: Low oxygen readings need a second person to confirm.

rules.title: Your mood has been lower than usual
rules.summary: Your check-ins have been lower than your own normal for a while. That is common on long, isolated missions and easier to turn around early.
rules.action: Book a private conversation: with the medical officer, or a recorded message to the support team at home.
steps: Put one thing you enjoy and one contact with home on today's plan.
Keep exercise and the sleep period fixed; both lift mood.
You control who sees this. Sharing it with the medical officer is one tap in Sharing.
rules.tier_reason: Private by default; you decide whether to involve anyone.

escalate.reason: Lasting ten days or more: Keel recommends sharing it with the medical officer.

rules.title: You are running short on sleep
rules.summary: Your sleep has been shorter or later than your own normal for several days. Sleep debt builds quietly and shows up first as slower reactions.
rules.action: Protect a full 8.5-hour sleep period tonight.
steps: Switch your quarters to the warm pre-sleep light setting two hours before bed.
Last caffeine at least six hours before sleep.
If the schedule moved, use bright light after waking to bring your body clock along.
Keep safety-critical tasks out of your 1 to 7 AM low, or ask for a buddy check.
rules.tier_reason: Usually fixed by protecting sleep for a few nights.

escalate.reason: Reaction time is now affected or the pattern has lasted six days: the medical officer can adjust the schedule or discuss sleep aids.

rules.title: You are drinking less than usual
rules.summary: Fluid intake is below your own normal, and your body is starting to show it. In space this also raises kidney-stone risk.
rules.action: Drink one extra litre before the end of the day, spread over the next few hours.
steps: Aim for 2.0 to 2.5 litres a day and pale urine.
Log each drink bag at check-in so the trend is visible.
Tell the medical officer about any sharp side or back pain.

rules.title: Exercise has dropped below your plan
rules.summary: Your weekly exercise is well under your own normal. Without gravity, fitness, muscle and bone are only held by daily loading, and the loss is silent.
rules.action: Do today's session, even a shortened one, and plan the next three.
steps: If a device is down, use the substitute session: elastic bands and bodyweight circuits.
If you are skipping because you feel unwell or low, say so at check-in so Keel can connect it.
Resting heart rate creeping up over the next weeks is the first sign of lost fitness.
rules.tier_reason: Getting back on plan is the countermeasure.

escalate.reason: Ten days below plan: the medical officer should adjust the prescription.

rules.title: You are eating less than planned
rules.summary: Food intake has been below your own normal. Under-eating in space speeds up loss of body mass, muscle and bone.
rules.action: Add one planned snack today and finish the main meals.
steps: Check body mass at the next scheduled measurement.
If food has lost its appeal or you feel nauseous, note it at check-in.

rules.title: Your reactions are slower than usual
rules.summary: Your reaction self-test is slower than your own normal without a clear sleep change.
rules.action: Repeat the test after a ten-minute break; if it is still slow, ask for a buddy check on critical tasks today.
steps: Check the cabin carbon dioxide reading on the Today screen.
Think about last night's sleep and today's workload.
rules.tier_reason: One slow test is common; a pattern matters.

rules.title: Your heart is working harder at rest
rules.summary: Resting heart rate or heart rate variability has moved away from your own normal without another clear signal.
rules.action: Ease today's exercise intensity and check the basics: fluids, sleep, workload.
steps: Take a two-minute still reading with the chest strap tomorrow after waking.
If it has not returned to your range in three days, Keel will suggest involving the medical officer.
rules.tier_reason: Often explained by sleep, fluids or training load.

escalate.reason: Not back in range after four days.

rules.title: Several readings have drifted from your normal
rules.summary: No single reading stands out, but taken together your numbers are unusual for you.
rules.action: Do a full check-in today and repeat any reading that looks wrong.
steps: Check that the wearable is snug and charged.
If you feel fine and it clears in two days, no action is needed.
rules.tier_reason: A combined drift without a clear pattern.

escalate.reason: Persisting for five days without explanation.
